rationales.1: Window sections, the month filter, sidebar links, and the twelve-cell sowing band make season fit glanceable, with price and stock in a steady position per entry.
rationales.2: The boxed buy panel with price, counted stock, quantity field, and a large Add to basket button is textbook convention, and the catalog keeps all cleverness away from the money path.
rationales.3: The estimated germination rate gets its own margin note explaining it is from last season's line, the sweet pea shows Price pending rather than a number, out of stock is plain, and UK-only shipping tops both surfaces.
rationales.4: Serif body text is generous, the buy button is large, nothing depends on hover, and the unlabeled month band is safely redundant with the written sowing months beside it.
rationales.5: The two-column page with italic margin notes, dotted rules, and a restrained plum and green palette holds together as one editorial system on both surfaces and in both modes.
rationales.6: The year band, sowing table, difficulty line, margin note, and companions are arranged so the first-time gardener's questions are answered in reading order without leaving the page.
rationales.7: Find your month first, then your packet is a one-sentence signature that structure, visualization, marginalia, and copy all genuinely enforce, and it is service culture true of a two-person seed shop.
rationales.8: The almanac novelty lives entirely in the brand and information layer while filtering, links, and the buy box stay strictly conventional.
rationales.9: Margin notes like takes an autumn sowing too, as the band shows, and the whole plant earns its bed are specific, unhurried, and unpublishable by a generic competitor.
rationales.10: A repeat visitor checking what is sowable now is served by the month-first structure, the bands, and visible stock states immediately, and the two surfaces cohere as one almanac.
